cases.sentence: Уже перед концом курса вод князь Щербацкий, ездивший после Карлсбада в Баден и Киссинген к русским знакомым набраться ___, как он говорил, вернулся к своим.
cases.explain: «русского духа» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Before the end of the course of drinking the waters, Prince Shtcherbatsky, who had gone on from Carlsbad to Baden and Kissingen to Russian friends—to get a breath of Russian air, as he said—came back to his wife and daughter.

cases.sentence: Князь же, напротив, находил за границей все скверным, тяготился европейской жизнью, держался своих ___ и нарочно старался выказывать себя за границей менее европейцем, чем он был в действительности.
cases.explain: «русских привычек» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: The views of the prince and of the princess on life abroad were completely opposed. The princess thought everything delightful, and in spite of her established position in Russian society, she tried abroad to be like a European fashionable lady, which she was not—for the simple reason that she was a typical Russian gentlewoman; and so she was affected, which did not altogether suit her. The prince, on the contrary, thought everything foreign detestable, got sick of European life, kept to his Russian habits, and purposely tried to show himself abroad less European than he was in reality.

cases.sentence: Но эти ___ потонули в том море добродушия и веселости, которые всегда были в нем и особенно усилились карлсбадскими водами.
cases.explain: «неприятные известия» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: The prince returned thinner, with the skin hanging in loose bags on his cheeks, but in the most cheerful frame of mind. His good humor was even greater when he saw Kitty completely recovered. The news of Kitty’s friendship with Madame Stahl and Varenka, and the reports the princess gave him of some kind of change she had noticed in Kitty, troubled the prince and aroused his habitual feeling of jealousy of everything that drew his daughter away from him, and a dread that his daughter might have got out of the reach of his influence into regions inaccessible to him. But these unpleasant matters were all drowned in the sea of kindliness and good humor which was always within him, and more so than ever since his course of Carlsbad waters.

cases.sentence: Но эти неприятные известия потонули в том море добродушия и веселости, которые всегда были в нем и особенно усилились ___.
cases.explain: «карлсбадскими водами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.

But these unpleasant matters were all drowned in the sea of kindliness and good humor which was always within him, and more so than ever since his course of Carlsbad waters.

cases.sentence: На другой день по своем приезде князь в своем ___, со своими русскими морщинами и одутловатыми щеками, подпертыми крахмаленными воротничками, в самом веселом расположении духа пошел с дочерью на воды.
cases.explain: «длинном пальто» — after the preposition «со», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The day after his arrival the prince, in his long overcoat, with his Russian wrinkles and baggy cheeks propped up by a starched collar, set off with his daughter to the spring in the greatest good humor.

cases.sentence: На другой день по своем приезде князь в своем длинном пальто, со своими ___ и одутловатыми щеками, подпертыми крахмаленными воротничками, в самом веселом расположении духа пошел с дочерью на воды.

cases.translation: The day after his arrival the prince, in his long overcoat, with his Russian wrinkles and baggy cheeks propped up by a starched collar, set off with his daughter to the spring in the greatest good humor.

cases.sentence: – Представь, представь меня своим ___, говорил он дочери, пожимая локтем ее руку. – Я и этот твой гадкий Соден полюбил за то, что он тебя так справил.
cases.explain: «новым друзьям» — the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Present me to your new friends,” he said to his daughter, squeezing her hand with his elbow. “I like even your horrid Soden for making you so well again. Only it’s melancholy, very melancholy here. Who’s that?”

cases.sentence: У ___ в сад они встретили слепую m-me Berthe с проводницей, и князь порадовался на умиленное выражение старой француженки когда она услыхала голос Кити.
cases.explain: «самого входа» — after the preposition «у», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Kitty mentioned the names of all the people they met, with some of whom she was acquainted and some not. At the entrance of the garden they met the blind lady, Madame Berthe, with her guide, and the prince was delighted to see the old Frenchwoman’s face light up when she heard Kitty’s voice. She at once began talking to him with French exaggerated politeness, applauding him for having such a delightful daughter, extolling Kitty to the skies before her face, and calling her a treasure, a pearl, and a consoling angel.

cases.sentence: У самого входа в сад они встретили слепую m-me Berthe с проводницей, и князь порадовался на умиленное выражение ___ когда она услыхала голос Кити.

cases.sentence: – Ну, так она ___, – сказал князь улыбаясь. – Она называет ангелом нумер первый mademoiselle Вареньку.
cases.explain: «второй ангел» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Well, she’s the second angel, then,” said the prince, smiling. “She calls Mademoiselle Varenka angel number one.”

cases.sentence: – Оh! M-lle Варенька – это ___, аllez, – подхватила m-me Berthe.
cases.explain: «настоящий ангел» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh! Mademoiselle Varenka, she’s a real angel, allez,” Madame Berthe assented.

cases.sentence: Какое ___! – спросил он, заметив сидевшего на лавочке невысокого больного в коричневом пальто и белых панталонах, делавших странные складки на лишенных мяса костях его ног.
cases.explain: «жалкое лицо» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Who’s that? What a piteous face!” he asked, noticing a sick man of medium height sitting on a bench, wearing a brown overcoat and white trousers that fell in strange folds about his long, fleshless legs. This man lifted his straw hat, showed his scanty curly hair and high forehead, painfully reddened by the pressure of the hat.

cases.sentence: Он подошел к мадам Шталь и заговорил на том отличном ___, на котором столь немногие уже говорят теперь, чрезвычайно учтиво и мило.
cases.explain: «французском языке» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: The prince went up to her, and Kitty detected that disconcerting gleam of irony in his eyes. He went up to Madame Stahl, and addressed her with extreme courtesy and affability in that excellent French that so few speak nowadays.

cases.sentence: – Да я уж привыкла, – сказала мадам Шталь и познакомила князя со ___.
cases.explain: «шведским графом» — after the preposition «со», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Yes; I’m used to it,” said Madame Stahl, and she introduced the prince to the Swedish count.

cases.sentence: – Это не нам судить, – сказала госпожа Шталь, заметив оттенок выражения на лице князя. – Так вы пришлете мне эту книгу, ___?
cases.explain: «любезный граф» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That is not for us to judge,” said Madame Stahl, perceiving the shade of expression on the prince’s face. “So you will send me that book, dear count? I’m very grateful to you,” she said to the young Swede.

cases.sentence: Очень благодарю вас, – обратилась она к ___.
cases.explain: «молодому шведу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “That is not for us to judge,” said Madame Stahl, perceiving the shade of expression on the prince’s face. “So you will send me that book, dear count? I’m very grateful to you,” she said to the young Swede.

cases.sentence: – А! – вскрикнул князь, увидав московского полковника, стоявшего около, и, поклонившись госпоже Шталь, отошел с дочерью и с присоединившимся к ним ___.
cases.explain: «московским полковником» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Ah!” cried the prince, catching sight of the Moscow colonel standing near, and with a bow to Madame Stahl he walked away with his daughter and the Moscow colonel, who joined them.

cases.sentence: – Это наша аристократия, князь! – с желанием быть насмешливым сказал ___, который был в претензии на госпожу Шталь за то, что она не была с ним знакома.
cases.explain: «московский полковник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That’s our aristocracy, prince!” the Moscow colonel said with ironical intention. He cherished a grudge against Madame Stahl for not making his acquaintance.

cases.sentence: – ___ так говорят, мой дружок.
cases.explain: «Дурные языки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That’s what wicked tongues say, my darling. And your Varenka catches it too,” he added. “Oh, these invalid ladies!”

cases.sentence: Осталась одна ___, которая лежит потому, что дурно сложена, и мучает безответную Вареньку за то, что та не так подвертывает ей плед.
cases.explain: «коротконогая женщина» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Kitty did not answer, not because she had nothing to say, but because she did not care to reveal her secret thoughts even to her father. But, strange to say, although she had so made up her mind not to be influenced by her father’s views, not to let him into her inmost sanctuary, she felt that the heavenly image of Madame Stahl, which she had carried for a whole month in her heart, had vanished, never to return, just as the fantastic figure made up of some clothes thrown down at random vanishes when one sees that it is only some garment lying there. All that was left was a woman with short legs, who lay down because she had a bad figure, and worried patient Varenka for not arranging her rug to her liking. And by no effort of the imagination could Kitty bring back the former Madame Stahl.
